title: PRD: Hypothesis-driven test harness and stop criteria for Optimize evals
creator: Alexandra Chen
description:
Context:
Optimize needs a more actionable eval pipeline that ties measurable regressions to a clear decision matrix (stop/hold/rollout) and that surfaces per-cohort failure modes. Current evals are metric-first and lack hypothesis framing — teams spend time triaging noise rather than following a reproducible experiment-to-action path.

Goal:
Define and deliver a PRD for a hypothesis-driven test harness for Optimize that: (1) formalizes how teams write hypotheses for model changes, (2) maps cohorts and sampling rules to required statistical power, (3) produces composite signals and per-metric significance tests, and (4) defines concrete A/B decision criteria and automated rollback/elevation triggers. Deliverables: PRD, acceptance criteria, prototype harness (pipeline + dashboards), pilot runs on 3 representative prompt-sets.

Scope:
In-scope: cohort stratification rules, statistical test selection (sequential/alpha-spending), composite signal construction, decision matrix for canaries/A-Bs, runbook for rollback/escalation, UI/Console mockups for evaluating results.
Out-of-scope: full integration with Dedicated autoscaling, experimental ML model retraining loops, long-term storage retention policy (can be followed-up).

Who benefits:
- PMs/ML engineers: faster actionable signals and fewer false positives.
- Platform/Optimize users: clearer rollout guidance and fewer surprises from long-tail regressions.

Success metrics:
- Reduction in average triage time for eval regressions by 40% in pilot teams.
- Pilot detects >90% of injected regressions in controlled tests while keeping false-positive rate < 5%.

Related artifacts:
- PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPT/Hypothesis+Driven+Test+Harness
- Prototype harness (spike): https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize-evals/pull/142
- Pilot dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/optimize/eval-pilot
acceptance_criteria: Cohort definitions and stratification rules documented with minimum sample sizes and power calculations for medium-effect (Cohen d ~0.3) scenarios.
Statistical test spec chosen (primary + fallback) with rationale (e.g., sequential permutation + alpha-spending) and documented Type I/II trade-offs.
Composite signal definition (weights and normalization) for quality, safety, and latency that can be computed per-cohort and overall.
Decision matrix for canary/A-B with clear thresholds: auto-stop, escalate-to-sre, proceed-to-rollout percentages and hold criteria.
Automated rollback triggers defined and implementable as console policies (e.g., sustained composite drop > X over Y windows) with runbook steps.
Prototype harness runs end-to-end on three distinct prompt-sets (chat, instruction-completion, reranking) and produces reproducible reports and dashboards.
Operator facing Console mockups for cohort selector, signal breakdown, and one-click rollback/annotate actions reviewed and approved by Design and SRE.
Pilot runbook that documents required infra, expected runtime, failure modes, and estimated compute/cost for a single full evaluation run.
decisions: Adopt hypothesis-first workflow: every candidate run must include one or more testable hypotheses with targeted cohorts.
Use stratified sequential testing to allow early stopping while controlling Type I error; fallback to fixed-sample tests when sequential assumptions not met.
Composite signal will weight safety higher than latency for customer-facing cohorts; default weights: safety 50%, quality 35%, latency 15% (tunable per project).
Rollbacks will be automated only for high-confidence stop signals (sustained composite drop + safety regression in top-priority cohort); otherwise raised to on-call with annotated triage checklist.
Pilot will ship as an optical layer on top of existing Optimize eval infra; runtime/perf improvements deferred to follow-up ENG spike.
